solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put on suit, slender thing

parts.note: to suit is to go with or match
to put something on, as a label, is to stick it on

explanation.surface: Someone dresses in a suit and is described as a slender thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is built in answer order, so the 'suit' word comes first although it is second in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin wooden stick tipped for striking a light is a typically slender object.

clue.text: Staff a cause of irritation

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial club or rod carried as a symbol of authority
a pepper-based spray that stings the eyes and skin

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an official's ceremonial rod and a tear-gas spray used to irritate attackers.

clue.text: Very little money on display, ultimately

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word display

explanation.surface: Hardly any cash is on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something minute or very small is very little.

clue.text: Try being popular on social media? That's sad

parts.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case in court
a topic that is suddenly popular online is said to be trending

explanation.surface: A wry remark that chasing online popularity is rather pathetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but it is the legal sense: to try a case is to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deeply distressing, which wrenches the emotions, is something that is sad.

clue.text: Giant ring worn by king

indicators.note: the ring word is worn around the king letter, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a bell rings or tolls
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wears a ring, perhaps one of great size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is the bell sense, not jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scandinavian folklore a troll is a giant or ogre-like creature.

clue.text: Altar cup I spilt, as cathedral official

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of the phrase are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy cleric confesses to knocking over the altar cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitular is a member of a cathedral chapter, the body of canons running it.

clue.text: Wanting backing, music scene that's flat

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the backing is the final letter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a disco is a dance music scene or venue

explanation.surface: A music scene without support is a dull, flat affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' suggests musical accompaniment, but it means the back end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a thin round object, so it is something flat.

clue.text: Artistic director breaking a promise to adopt case of Rossini

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the shuffled letters enclose the outer pair
breaking a promise here means the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A theatre boss goes back on a promise to stage a Rossini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges A PROMISE to IMPRESAO, and 'to adopt' takes RI, the outside of Rossini, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a manager or producer of operas, concerts or plays, an arts director.

clue.text: Test tin in gateau that's poisoning animal

indicators.note: in places the test and tin letters inside the cake word

parts.note: a gateau is a rich cake
an oral is a spoken exam
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Someone tests a gateau for tin contamination that has poisoned an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous American serpent can kill with its bite, so it is a poisonous creature.

clue.text: Tin brownish-grey, look inside for fruit

parts.note: a can is a tin container

indicators.note: inside puts the look letters within the colour word

parts.note: taupe is a brownish-grey colour
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Peer into a dull grey tin to find some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of melon with orange flesh, so an example of fruit.

clue.text: Post box

definitions.meaning: a pole or stout length of timber
to box is to practise fighting with a partner

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stout pole, as on a ship, and to practise boxing.

clue.text: Gossip is written about model, not quite all there

indicators.note: written about means the gossip word is set around the shortened model word

parts.note: comment here is idle chat or remarks about others

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle surrounds a model who seems a little dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite all there' looks like the definition, but 'not quite' shortens the model word, and 'written about' wraps the gossip round it; only 'all there' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means of sound mind, which is the idiom 'all there'.

clue.text: Foreign article behind the toilets melting — might it ruin the carpet?

indicators.note: behind places the foreign article after the rearranged letters
melting suggests the letters of the phrase lose their shape and re-form

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A grim scene of something foreign near melting toilets, with fears for the carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting' gives STILETTOHE, and 'behind' puts the Spanish article after it; the whole clue paints the scene, with the question as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, spiked high heel on a woman's shoe is notorious for piercing floor coverings.

clue.text: A giant among poets?

parts.note: a tall man is a lanky chap, and the American who wrote Hiawatha bears that description as his surname

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the surname describes a tall man, so the poet is literally a 'giant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American poet Henry Wadsworth, author of Hiawatha, bore this surname, which also describes a tall man.

clue.text: Canny way letters read out

parts.note: a street is a road or way

indicators.note: read out means the letters are spoken, giving a word with that sound

parts.note: the letters in question are Ys, more than one letter Y

explanation.surface: A clever way of reading letters aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' turns YS, two of the letter Y, into its spoken sound, a word for sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrewd in the ways of modern urban life is canny, sharp and worldly.

clue.text: Dribbling while awake?

definitions.meaning: a footballer dribbling keeps control of the football at their feet

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means alert and sharp, while literally describing a player keeping the football close.

clue.text: Order in bad way, euros heading for extinction

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the two words are in poor order and must be rearranged
heading for points to the first letter of the word extinction

explanation.surface: The single currency is in a bad way and heading for extinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges WAY EUROS into ASYOUWER, and 'heading for' adds E, the start of extinction.
explanation.definitionFit: This military command tells soldiers to return to their previous position, so it is an order.

clue.text: Filling empty pan, uncooked seafood

indicators.note: filling means the uncooked word goes inside the emptied pan
empty means the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: Fill an empty pan with raw seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A small edible shellfish is a type of seafood.

clue.text: Avidity does good? The reverse!

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the does-plus-good letters backwards

parts.note: does are female deer, and the plural of deer is unchanged

explanation.surface: Asking whether eagerness does good, and answering that it does the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb, but it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidity is keen eagerness, and its excessive form is avarice or acquisitiveness.

clue.text: Standard criticism applied to enclosed space

indicators.note: applied to puts the criticism word after the space word

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed area beside a building
stick is informal for criticism, as in 'taking stick'

explanation.surface: A standard criticism made of a cramped space.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark or criterion for measuring things is a standard.

clue.text: Put out nightie, used around about ten

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the ten letter
around suggests the letters are moved round into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a used nightie at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives ETINGUISHED, and 'about' wraps that round the Roman ten; 'around about' reads as one vague time phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a fire or light is to quench or douse it.

clue.text: Keep mum drinking mother's ruin!

indicators.note: drinking means the silence word takes the mother's letters inside it

parts.note: sh is the call for silence, telling someone to keep mum
ma is mother, so mother's is ma's

explanation.surface: Someone hushes up a mother who is drinking gin.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mother's ruin" is British slang for gin, and the drinking suggests it, but 'ruin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to wreck or destroy something is to ruin it.

clue.text: Nick's head taken off — duck!

indicators.note: head taken off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A warning to duck before Nick is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small freshwater dabbling species of wildfowl, so a kind of duck.

clue.text: Other similar things additionally beginning to hurt, dig deep?

indicators.note: additionally means the next letter is added on after

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other similar things

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word hurt

explanation.surface: More things start to hurt as you dig deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut deep lines into a surface, as acid does on a plate.

clue.text: Hide Asian currency, turning back

indicators.note: turning back reads the currency word in reverse

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and some Gulf states

explanation.surface: Hide some Asian money and turn back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is a hiding place, and a den is a lair.

clue.text: Leave me not without love in office

parts.note: to depart is to leave

indicators.note: without removes the love letter from the word not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A plea not to be left alone in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A government ministry or a section of an organisation is an office.

clue.text: Little break's ending in a few days

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: ending points to the last letter of the break word

explanation.surface: A short break lasting a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of seven days is a fair, if loose, meaning of a few days.

clue.text: Very old man me, so fit to go back

parts.note: thus means so, in that way

indicators.note: to go back means the fit word is reversed

parts.note: hale means fit and healthy

explanation.surface: An elderly man reckons he is so fit he can go back.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years is the byword for great age.
